bugs.summary: C stack checking silently disabled when stack limit > 100MB (FreeBSD default), causing segfaults
bugs.creator: jeroenooms

comments.creator: jeroenooms
comments.text:
Created attachment 4053
fix stack limit

setup_Rmainloop() in src/main/main.c discards any C stack limit above
1e8 bytes:

  if(R_CStackLimit > 100000000U)
      R_CStackLimit = (uintptr_t)-1;

which turns off all C stack checking, including R_CheckStack2(). The
default stack limit on FreeBSD is 512MB, so on a stock FreeBSD system
Cstack_info() returns NA and stack overflows segfault instead of raising
an error. In particular, tests/reg-tests-1e.R crashes in the PR#19188
test: format("é", width = 2^31 - 3) allocates a ~2GB VLA in do_format()
that R_CheckStack2() should reject.

This reproduces on Linux:

  $ ulimit -s 524288
  $ Rscript -e 'format("é", width = 2^31 - 3)'
   *** caught segfault ***

whereas with the default 8MB limit it gives
"C stack usage ... is too close to the limit".

The comment says the check exists for bogus limits and for 32-bit
platforms, where casting to intptr_t needs the limit to be below 2^31.
On 64-bit platforms a large limit is real. The attached patch keeps the
existing behaviour on 32-bit platforms. On 64-bit platforms it caps the
limit at INT_MAX instead of disabling the checks, which keeps
Cstack_info()'s int result in range.

Crash logs on FreeBSD before this patch: https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/actions/runs/43285958432/job/131419332100
Success on FreeBSD after this patch: https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/actions/runs/43383903100/job/131747763356
